title: Walk-Encoded Graph Descriptions in the Prompt
subtitle: Two Pilots and a Larger Run That Cannot Separate Structure from Content
abstract: Version 1.1 (correction, in preparation). Text descriptions of knowledge graphs in a model's system prompt, keyword-scored, on Qwen3-30B-A3B. In the larger run a walk-encoded description of the lab's memory graph raised multi-hop accuracy from 0.005 to 0.472, a hand-written paragraph containing every expected answer term (but not every path the questions ask for) to 0.676, unrelated prose 0.003; 36% and 20% of those arms' multi-hop replies were empty, and the arms differ in content, length and format at once, so structure is not isolated. A scrambled-label pilot (6 questions) is suggestive, not significant (paired p = 0.125, two-sided). Every condition gives the graph as text, and the lab's stored attempts at a graph-built cache scored nothing; version 1.0's cache-injection framing, and the companion study's claims it relied on, are withdrawn, and its results table, whose absolute values no data file contains, is corrected.
